sections.overview: Phyllobates aurotaenia, the Kokoe Poison Frog, is a poison frog endemic to western Colombia.
sections.identification: Its dorsal pattern varies; the species is a member of the genus Phyllobates, whose frogs include conspicuously striped forms.
sections.habitat: It inhabits wet forests in Colombia’s Chocó region, within the San Juan drainage.
sections.diet: A Colombian stomach-content study recorded varied prey, including aquatic and terrestrial organisms at different life stages.
sections.behavior: Field researchers have described its courtship, aggressive interactions and mating call.
sections.reproduction: A mating-call and courtship study documents reproductive behavior, but the sources used here do not summarize its full life cycle.
sections.ecology: A 2024 taxonomic revision separated southern populations formerly included in P. aurotaenia as Phyllobates samperi.
sections.conservation: A Colombian regional plan lists it as Least Concern; that category should be revisited alongside the recent taxonomic split.
